title: onprem upgrade failure autoremediation and customer escalation runbook
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: Multiple customers on Private/VPC reported upgrade failures during an automated operator/Helm chart rollout to private-operator v2.4.1. Symptoms included operator crashloops, NodeAgent not reconciling, and control-plane reconciliation timeouts. This ticket tracks diagnosis, a minimal hotfix release, and the customer-facing runbook for remediation and communication.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Install private-operator v2.3.x in a VPC cluster with existing managed secrets and legacy CRD variants
2) Run Helm upgrade to private-operator v2.4.1 with values.yaml used by customer's CI/CD
3) Observe operator controller logs: template rendering errors mentioning missing .Values.agentConfig, webhook registration failures, and crashloop restarts
4) Observe NodeAgent pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff and failing to create expected ConfigMaps
technical_root_cause: A template variable rename in the chart (agentConfig -> nodeAgent.config) combined with an optional CRD field change caused Helm to render manifests missing expected fields. The operator's controller code assumed the older schema and crashed while reconciling the missing keys. In clusters where the customer had manual overrides to the nodeagent secret or the CRD had a prior schema version, the operator applied partial updates resulting in config drift and webhook registration failures.
mitigation_steps: 1) Immediate: Pause automated upgrades for affected customers until hotfix is applied (see customer bucket list in links).

2) Hotfix: Publish chart patch and operator image that includes backward-compatible parsing (compat layer) and a one-shot migration job to reconcile missing fields (operator image tag private-operator:2.4.1-patch1).
3) Run migration: Provide a helm hook Job (reconcile-migration-job) that validates CRD versions, fills missing defaults, and ensures webhooks are registered before finalizing the upgrade.
4) Postfix: Add validation webhook with clearer errors (fail-fast) and pre-upgrade schema check in the upgrade CI to warn customers.
5) Customer-facing: Send runbook steps and offer hands-on remediation support for high-severity customers.
rollback_plan: If hotfix fails or customer prefers rollback, run Helm rollback to previous release (v2.3.x), restore operator replicas to previous image, and run a patchextract script to revert CRD schema changes. For clusters with irreversible migrations, escalate to SRE for live assistance. Rollback playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Onprem+Rollback+Playbook
acceptance_criteria: Operator stable (no crashloops) on previously-failing clusters after applying patch
NodeAgent reconciles and ConfigMaps/Secrets match expected templates
Automated CI pre-upgrade schema check blocks unsafe upgrades with clear error message
Customer confirmation from top 3 affected accounts that their workloads are restored
comments: 2026-03-11 Priya Nambiar: Initial triage - reproduced locally with a minikube cluster and legacy CRD. Observed missing rendered fields in Helm manifest. Assigned to Luca for patch and migration job.
2026-03-12 Luca Martinez: Implemented compatibility parsing in operator; created migration Job. Filed PRs for operator + chart. Need QA on customers with manual secret overrides.
2026-03-13 QA (Neha Patel): Verified patch on two customer-like clusters. One edge-case where manual secret was encrypted by external KMS required manual secret unwrap step; documented in runbook.
2026-03-14 PM (Marco Silva): Drafted customer email and support playbook for high-impact accounts. Recommend immediate outreach and scheduled remediation windows.
2026-03-14 SRE (Ava Johnson): Added pre-upgrade validation to the operator helm release CI and circuit-breaker to pause cluster auto-upgrades if webhook registration fails more than 3 times.
resolution_summary: Hotfix release private-operator:2.4.1-patch1 and charts PR merged. Migration job added as a Helm hook to populate renamed fields and re-register webhooks safely. Pre-upgrade schema validation and a temporary auto-upgrade pause policy were enabled. Top three affected customers restored within SLA; remaining customers scheduled for remediation windows. Follow-up: write automated migration unit tests and add KMS-aware secret handling to migration job. Postmortem planned in two weeks.
postmortem_notes: Root cause was a chart variable rename that lacked a compatibility shim and insufficient pre-upgrade validation. Contributing factors: manual secret overrides at customer clusters and lack of CI tests against older CRD variants. Action items: 1) Add backward-compat parsers and unit tests, 2) Add pre-upgrade schema check to release pipeline, 3) Improve communications for upgrade windows, 4) Update onboarding docs for secret management.
